title: Sparsify-then-steer: how few dimensions does a safety steering vector really need?

original_idea.body: Greedily sparsify CAA vectors for 4 safety concepts and plot per-concept sparsity-retention curves to find which concepts are genuinely low-dimensional.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible interpretability/tamper-resistance chain, but the link to catastrophic-risk reduction is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CAA extraction + greedy top-k sparsification + effect measurement; standard tools, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: sparsity-retention curves for 4 concepts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Self-contained interpretability result, public data, no internal access; externally doable.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap vector ops on one model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Sparsification shown for refusal; extending to other safety concepts is a partly-open generalization.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sparsification was shown for refusal; whether other safety concepts are equally sparse is a partly-open extension.
